_measured: Every `min_sites` floor below was set by running that rule's own locator against the real corpus on dev, never by estimate. Measured 2026-07-29: http-stack-justified-crates 8, architecture-map-crate-label 430, vendor-lockin-seam 26, markdown-cargo-p 1666, build-target-label 327, decision-record-crate-refs 28. Census: 897 workspace packages, 1480 names after the lockfile union.
_comment: cloud-ci-crate-reference-integrity (ADR-0630). Every structural site class at which a governed artifact NAMES a crate is one object in `rules` below; adding a site TYPE is a data edit here and never a code change. `kind` is a closed enum of collector SHAPES, and only a genuinely new shape needs Rust. TWO deliberate non-registrations, recorded so a future reader does not 'fix' them: (1) the per-rule glob field is named `file_globs`, NOT a coverage-bearing key (`roots` / `scan_roots` / `crate_root_globs` / `manifest_paths` / `store_manifest_paths`), so cloud-ci-scan-root-liveness does not collect it — and does not need to, because this gate's own `rule_glob_matches_nothing` is strictly stronger than an existence check: it also fails when a glob resolves but the structural locator behind it yields nothing. (2) There is no `--fix`: a dangling reference has three legitimate resolutions and the third one is 'this is a dated record that must NOT be rewritten', which an autofixer gets wrong by construction. See gate-self-conformance `no_autofix_reason`. NO RULE MAY CARRY A ZERO FLOOR: an earlier draft declared the decision-record rule dormant on a measurement that matched only at column 0 and therefore missed 25 files whose `crates:` key is nested under `affected_surfaces` and indented; a declared-but-unmeasured rule is the exact false-green this gate exists to stop, so `min_sites: 0` is itself a violation.

rules.subject: package_name
rules.reason: justified_crates.<framework> is KEYED BY PACKAGE NAME; a moved crate strands its justification and the http-stack gate silently stops covering it.

rules.subject: package_name
rules.reason: the generated architecture graph labels crate nodes by package name. A stale PATH PREFIX around a live package name (the dead `microservices/...` ids) is a different defect — path liveness — and is deliberately out of scope.

rules.subject: package_name_last_path_segment
rules.reason: seam declarations store the adapter crate as a PATH whose last segment is the package name, alongside free text like 'GitHub (current impl)' in the same field — which is why the name-shape filter is load-bearing rather than cosmetic.

rules.subject: package_name
rules.reason: a RUNNABLE command left broken. A reader copies it and it fails, and no compiler will ever tell them why.

rules.subject: build_target_label
rules.reason: a `//path:target` label resolves iff `path/<build_file>` exists in the tracked tree. Both filters are mandatory and both were measured: without the root-dir allowlist and the preceding-character rule, `//localhost:8080`, `//127.0.0.1:2379` and `//prometheus.oya-observability.svc:9090` all read as labels.

rules.subject: package_name
rules.reason: a decision record declares its affected crates in frontmatter, NESTED under affected_surfaces and therefore indented — which is why this is parsed structurally and why a column-anchored measurement wrongly concluded the field did not exist. `verified_by` is deliberately NOT read here: its values are gate ids and command phrases which are kebab-shaped but are not packages, so reading it would manufacture false positives rather than find defects.

_exclusions_note: Exclusions are shrink-only and staleness-checked: one that matches no tracked file, suppresses no would-be finding, or carries an empty reason is RED. `third-party/**` and `docs/audit/retired-workflows/**` were both drafted here and both REMOVED before landing because they were measured to suppress ZERO findings — a plausible-sounding exclusion that buys nothing today silently licenses everything that lands under it tomorrow.
